Definition: ; a prolonged form of a primary πλέω (which appears only as an alternate in certain tenses and in the reduplicated form πίμπλημι); to "fill" (literally or figuratively (imbue, influence, supply)); specially, to fulfil (time):--accomplish, full (…come), furnish.
BiblicalUsage: Pletho means to be filled, filled up to the full. John the Baptist would be filled with the Holy Ghost from his mother's womb, in Luke 1:15, and Zacharias was filled with the Holy Ghost and prophesied in Luke 1:67. On Pentecost they were all filled with the Holy Ghost in Acts 2:4, and Peter, filled with the Holy Ghost, spoke boldly in Acts 4:8. When they prayed, the place was shaken, and they were all filled again in Acts 4:31.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe being filled is not a once-for-all event but an again-and-again grace — the disciples were filled, and filled again. That is why I hold that I should keep asking, because God keeps filling.
RelatedTopics: Outpouring of the Spirit; Boldness; Prayer
